title: Perchway Systems - Implementation Kickoff
summary: Introductory kickoff to align on Perchway's inference use cases, infra constraints (VPC/on-prem), security checklist (SOC2, SSO, KMS), pilot scope (10k queries/day), and next steps including a benchmark run and security packet delivery.
topics: deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private
security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood), Rina (Redwood), Liam (Redwood), Tom (Perchway), Jia (Perchway), Sunil (Perchway), Marta (Perchway)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time. quick intros, then we'll walk the plan for kickoff.
[00:14] Tom: Hey Ava. Thanks, excited to get started. We have Tom, Jia, Sunil and Marta on our side. We're the Perchway team working on the AI assistant for ops.
[00:24] Rina: Hi all — Rina here, solutions engineer. I'll cover infra and pilot measurement stuff.
[00:31] Liam: Liam — CS lead, here to help with runbooks and onboarding cadence.
[00:36] Sunil: Sunil, CTO. My main concern is data residency and latency for edge customers.

[02:05] Ava: Cool, goal for today is to confirm scope, hand off the infra intake, and agree next steps. Can you, Tom, just run through what success looks like for you in three months?
[02:18] Tom: Sure. So the quick version — goal is 10k queries/day in production on our support flow, <200ms model latency target for search prompts and sub-second for light completions. Also need audit logging for compliance. We want to avoid building scale infra ourselves.
[02:48] Marta: And for product ops, we need the ability to rollback model changes and run small A/Bs.
[03:10] Rina: That aligns. For rollback and rollouts we support canaries and A/B via the rollout policies in the console. We can show that in the demo.

[05:00] Jia: Network question first — we run mostly in GCP but some customers are in private colo. Can Redwood support VPC peering and an on-prem connector?
[05:12] Rina: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and we have an on-prem package. For the hosted option we do TLS over the internet; for private deployments we can configure private endpoints. Note: V-P-C setup sometimes requires firewall egress rules to allow the runtime to hit our control plane (or vice versa) — we'll produce a network diagram.
[06:03] Sunil: KMS and key separation — can we bring our own key? We need HSM-backed key material for PII logs.
[06:12] Rina: Yep, BYOK via K-M-S integration is supported for Private; for Dedicated we can also integrate with customer KMS and we produce audit logs for request IDs. There was a small mis-say earlier in the docs where they said KVS but it's KV cache - sorry, transcription of docs sometimes says "KV cash" — but that's just the cache.

[08:20] Ava: On pricing and pilot sizing, you're expecting a pilot throughput and then a ramp. Tom said 10k queries/day — do we have an estimate of tokens per request?
[08:34] Tom: Roughly 1.2k tokens for a long support conversation, average ~320 tokens. Most are embeddings for retrieval and then short completions.
[08:47] Rina: That informs batching and model selection. We usually recommend a mid-sized encoder for embeddings and an LLM for the assistant; if latency is tight we'll suggest a quantized variant on Dedicated or Private to cut costs.

[10:15] Marta: Security pack — SSO and SAML is mandatory for us, plus SOC2 attestation. Are those available out of box?
[10:25] Liam: We support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning. We'll share the SSO runbook. Redwood is SOC2 compliant; we'll attach the certs and the evidence package in the security packet.
[11:04] Jia: Also need to know about data retention and search logs. How long do you keep transcripts by default?
[11:12] Rina: Hosted retains short-term by default, but with Private you control retention and can disable storage of transcripts entirely. We'll note that in the security doc.

[13:00] Tom: For benchmarks — we'd like a synthetic workload that simulates our query distribution. Can Redwood run a benchmark against our models in our VPC?
[13:13] Rina: We can run a benchmark partner-side. Option A: run inside your VPC with our agent for Private; Option B: simulate load against hosted/dedicated. If you want realistic KV cache behavior we prefer running in an environment that mirrors production.
[14:00] Sunil: Latency vs cost — what's the tradeoff? We burn money on sub-second SLOs.
[14:08] Rina: There are levers: batching, prefix caching (KV cache), model quantization, and routing to cheaper variants for non-critical paths. We'll show a cost/latency profile for your token distribution.

[16:35] Ava: Let's capture milestones: week 1 infra intake, week 2 benchmark, week 3 initial pilot, then weekly syncs. Is that timeline realistic?
[16:50] Tom: Yes, assuming we get network and SSO details in 48 hours.

[18:05] Marta: Who does the infra intake? We have internal networking folks who won't be in every call.
[18:12] Liam: Liam - CS will own the intake coordination. We'll share an intake form for VPC and firewall rules.

[20:20] Jia: A couple of technical deep-dive requests: 1) We need details on how KV cache is persisted, 2) how rollback of model versions is implemented, 3) whether the runtime supports continuous batching for mixed-length requests.
[20:38] Rina: We can schedule a SE deep-dive. Briefly: KV cache is in-memory per runtime instance with optional warm-start snapshotting for Private, rollbacks are through model pinning and immediate fallback policies, and continuous batching is a core runtime feature — there are knobs to tune target batch sizes to balance latency. I'll put the deep dive on the calendar.

[23:00] Tom: Any constraints around compliance scanning or pen testing access? We do third-party scans.
[23:12] Ava: We'll provide the redwood security packet; for pen testing we have a standard process — you submit the scope and we coordinate a window, plus we require notification for control-plane tests.

[25:45] Rina: Quick demo note: when we demo rollout policies you can see per-route stats, token-level cost, and we can wire your telemetry (Datadog/Prometheus) to the tracing hooks.
[26:10] Jia: Good — we use Datadog.

[28:00] Speaker 1: (overlap) — can you do private on-prem install in an air-gapped environment?
[28:08] Rina: Short answer: yes, our on-prem package supports air-gapped installs but requires additional ops coordination and a different licensing agreement. We'll include the on-prem checklist.

[30:40] Sunil: For rollouts, can we run A/B tests and pushback to previous model if we see quality regression?
[30:52] Rina: Yes — automatic fallback on degradation is supported if you configure the regression thresholds. We'll document example alert settings.

[33:00] Tom: A question about observability retention — can we get token-level cost for each route?
[33:08] Liam: Yes, per-route and per-model dashboards exist; we can provision a dashboard and share access.

[35:20] Ava: Ok, let's surface blockers now. Anything preventing us from starting the infra intake this week?
[35:29] Jia: Need security approval for us to share private VPC IP ranges with Redwood.
[35:35] Sunil: Also need SSO details from our identity team.

[37:00] Ava: Action: we'll send the intake form and the security packet. Can you agree to have the security team respond by Thursday?
[37:10] Sunil: We'll try; likely within 72 hours.

[39:00] Marta: On the product side, we want the ability to flag model versions with experiment names for tracking.
[39:12] Rina: We have metadata tagging for model versions; we can show how to tag and query performance per experiment.

[41:20] Tom: For pilot acceptance, what are the pass/fail criteria?
[41:30] Ava: Proposed: 1) Functional correctness baseline on 1k labeled prompts (>= 85% quality), 2) latency SLOs met 95% of requests, 3) stable logging and rollbacks demonstrated. We can iterate.

[44:00] Jia: Ok, can you share a sample SOW for a 3-month pilot and pricing ranges?
[44:08] Ava: Yes — I'll send a tailored SOW and a price worksheet for hosted vs dedicated vs private. Expect that in 48 hours.

[45:15] Tom: Great. Any blockers on Redwood's side?
[45:20] Liam: Nothing major — we need the intake details and security response.

[46:10] Ava: Recap: intake form + security packet sent today; Perchway to respond with network and SSO details within 72 hours; Redwood to run a benchmark afterwards and schedule a technical deep dive. We'll set weekly syncs. Thanks all.
[46:40] Tom: Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
action_items: Ava Martinez | Send tailored SOW and hosted/dedicated/private pricing worksheet | 2025-07-24
Liam O'Connor | Share VPC/network intake form and SSO runbook | 2025-07-22
Rina Patel | Schedule SE technical deep-dive on KV cache, rollbacks, and batching; prepare demo artifacts | 2025-07-28
Perchway - Ja Lin (Platform) | Provide VPC IP ranges, firewall rules, and SSO metadata | 2025-07-25
Perchway - Security Team | Review security packet and confirm pen-test window or constraints | 2025-07-25
next_steps: Redwood to send security packet and SOC2 attestation bundle (today)
Perchway to provide network and SSO details within 72 hours
Schedule SE deep-dive to run after intake is complete (week of 2025-07-28)
Run benchmark in environment chosen by Perchway and share results
Weekly syncs to be scheduled — first one one week from today
